source.original_text: For natural d and q with 2q+1<d, put r=q+1. Let g_1,...,g_r be independent standard Gaussian vectors in real d-dimensional Euclidean space, realized on their column-product probability space. For each physical coordinate i=1,...,d, form the row vector gamma_i=(g_1i,...,g_ri) in real r-dimensional Euclidean space. The full family gamma_1,...,gamma_d is independent. This independence subclaim means factorization of probabilities of finite intersections of measurable row events. The Gaussian marginal-law subclaim is kept in its existing canonical declaration.

blind_reconstruction.text:
# Source-blind mathematical reconstruction

For every pair of nonnegative integers d and q satisfying 2q + 1 < d, let D be real d-dimensional Euclidean space and let E be real (q + 1)-dimensional Euclidean space, each with its Borel measurable structure. Let gamma_D be the centered Gaussian probability measure on D with identity covariance. On Omega = D^{Fin(q + 1)}, equip the tuple omega = (omega(a))_{a in Fin(q + 1)} with the product probability measure mu = product_{a in Fin(q + 1)} gamma_D. For each i in Fin d define R_i : Omega -> E by (R_i(omega))_a = (omega(a))_i for every a in Fin(q + 1). Then the entire family (R_i)_{i in Fin d} is mutually independent with respect to mu.

Explicitly, for every subset S of Fin d and every choice of Borel sets A_i contained in E for i in S,

  mu({omega in Omega : R_i(omega) belongs to A_i for every i in S})
    = product_{i in S} mu({omega in Omega : R_i(omega) belongs to A_i}).

Every S is finite. For S empty, the event is Omega and the product is 1.

## Objects

D = EuclideanSpace R (Fin d) is the space of each sampled vector. E = EuclideanSpace R (Fin(q + 1)) is the target space of each row vector. Omega = Fin(q + 1) -> D is the tuple space of q + 1 sampled vectors. gamma_D = stdGaussian D is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability measure on D. mu is the finite product of q + 1 copies of gamma_D. For every coordinate i in Fin d, R_i(omega) collects that coordinate from all q + 1 sampled vectors, in their index order. WithLp.toLp 2 only wraps this coordinate function as an element of E; its coordinates do not change.

## Domains

d and q range over the nonnegative integers. The hypothesis implies d >= 2q + 2, so d >= 2; q = 0 is allowed. The sample index a belongs to Fin(q + 1) = {0,...,q}; the row index i belongs to Fin d = {0,...,d-1}. A point omega assigns a vector omega(a) in D to each sample index a. Each R_i maps Omega into E. D and E carry the Euclidean/Borel structures, and Omega carries the product measurable structure. The probability measure is mu on Omega. Target events A_i in the expanded conclusion are Borel subsets of E.

## Quantifiers

The theorem is universal in d and q and in a proof hq of 2 * q + 1 < d. These are not existentially chosen dimensions. After these quantifiers, D, E, Omega, mu, and R are fixed by local definitions, not universally quantified arbitrary spaces, measures, or maps. Mutual independence quantifies over every finite selected set S of row indices and every choice of measurable target event A_i for each selected i. Because Fin d is finite, this includes all subsets of the full row index set and, in particular, the full family. There are no existential witnesses or additional free parameters.

## Assumptions

The explicit dimension hypothesis is 2 * q + 1 < d. The natural-number domains and the given definitions supply all remaining context: real Euclidean spaces with Borel structures, the centered identity-covariance Gaussian measure on D, and its q + 1-fold product measure. The maps R_i are exactly the coordinate-collection maps in the statement. The Gaussian and product-measure specifications are part of the construction of mu, not assumptions about an arbitrary measure that could be varied independently. No separate measurability hypothesis is present.

## Conclusion

The single displayed conclusion is iIndepFun R mu: full mutual finite-family independence of the E-valued row maps (R_i)_{i in Fin d}. It gives the selected-event intersection/product identity displayed above for arbitrary Borel target sets, and therefore includes the full d-member family, not merely pairs. The product factors in that identity are the individual probabilities under mu; they are not replaced in the statement by stdGaussian E probabilities. There is no separately stated marginal-law conclusion such as (R_i)_*mu = stdGaussian E, nor any assertion that the row laws are identical. The construction specifies standard Gaussian factor laws on D for the sampled vectors omega(a); that input specification must not be conflated with an explicit output law for R_i in E. There is also no separate output Measurable R_i, AEMeasurable R_i, or joint measurability assertion. Under the supplied definition, iIndepFun alone does not assert measurability of arbitrary maps. No such extra conclusion is added here.

## Scopes

All local definitions occur inside the universal d, q, hq scope. D depends on d. E depends on q. Omega uses q + 1 copies of D and therefore depends on d and q. mu is defined on this Omega using stdGaussian D in every factor. R is the entire indexed family Fin d -> Omega -> E, with a the target/sample coordinate and i the sampled-vector coordinate. The family-independence assertion is made under this particular mu. The hypothesis hq restricts the permitted dimensions but is not an argument of any coordinate formula or measure definition. The event-product quantifiers concern target sets for selected row indices only; they do not introduce another probability measure or a different family of maps. The theorem makes no assertion for dimensions outside its stated bound, and the reconstruction makes no claim about necessity or sharpness of that bound.

## Constant dependencies

The only dimension parameters are d and q, restricted by 2 * q + 1 < d. The numerals 2 and 1 in that bound and the offset 1 in q + 1 are fixed literal constants. The 2 in WithLp.toLp 2 is the fixed Euclidean exponent, not another parameter. gamma_D is determined by D, hence by d. E is determined by q. Omega, mu, and the indexed row construction are determined by d and q and the fixed real Euclidean/Gaussian structures. There are no additional universal, existential, unspecified, dimension-dependent, tolerance, tail, error, or asymptotic constants, and no quantitative estimate or constant-dependence conclusion.

## Evidence boundary

This reconstruction uses only the anonymous Lean statement and the five approved definitions in input.json. It does not identify a source, declaration, original theorem, intended proof, or source-facing fidelity verdict. The packet reports that the anonymous statement compiled; this run did not independently compile or inspect a proof.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceRowLaw
import Mathlib.Probability.Independence.Basic
import Mathlib.Probability.ProductMeasure

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceRowLaw
set_option autoImplicit false

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceRowIndependence

theorem actual_source_rows_independent
    {d q : ℕ} (hq : 2 * q + 1 < d) :
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun a : Fin (q + 1) => ω a i)
  iIndepFun row μ := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let Q := Fin (q + 1)
  let I := Fin d
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ I
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ Q
  let Ω := Q → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Q => stdGaussian D)
  let row : I → Ω → E := fun i ω => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun a : Q => ω a i)
  let σ : Measure ℝ := gaussianReal 0 1
  let ν : Measure (Q → I → ℝ) :=
    Measure.pi (fun _ : Q => Measure.pi (fun _ : I => σ))
  let ρ : Measure (I → Q → ℝ) :=
    Measure.pi (fun _ : I => Measure.pi (fun _ : Q => σ))
  change iIndepFun row μ
  have row_law := actual_source_row_marginal_law (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change ∀ i : I, MeasurePreserving (row i) μ (stdGaussian E) at row_law

  -- The full physical-coordinate product law, not merely scalar marginals.
  have column_product :
      Measure.map (WithLp.toLp 2 : (I → ℝ) → D)
        (Measure.pi (fun _ : I => σ)) = stdGaussian D :=
    map_pi_eq_stdGaussian
  have unwrap_column :
      MeasurePreserving (fun x : D => fun i : I => x i)
        (stdGaussian D) (Measure.pi (fun _ : I => σ)) := by
    have hm : Measurable (fun x : D => fun i : I => x i) := by
      dsimp [D]
      fun_prop
    refine ⟨hm, ?_⟩
    rw [← column_product, Measure.map_map hm (by fun_prop)]
    change Measure.map id (Measure.pi (fun _ : I => σ)) = _
    exact Measure.map_id
  have unwrap_columns :
      MeasurePreserving (fun ω : Ω => fun a : Q => fun i : I => ω a i) μ ν :=
    measurePreserving_pi (fun _ : Q => stdGaussian D)
      (fun _ : Q => Measure.pi (fun _ : I => σ)) (fun _ => unwrap_column)

  -- Flatten, permute the two finite indices, and regroup the same scalar array.
  have flatten :
      MeasurePreserving (MeasurableEquiv.curry Q I ℝ).symm ν
        (Measure.pi (fun _ : Q × I => σ)) := by
    refine ⟨(MeasurableEquiv.curry Q I ℝ).symm.measurable, ?_⟩
    simpa only [Measure.infinitePi_eq_pi] using
      (Measure.infinitePi_map_curry_symm (fun (_ : Q) (_ : I) => σ))
  have swap :=
    measurePreserving_piCongrLeft (α := fun _ : I × Q => ℝ)
      (fun _ : I × Q => σ) (Equiv.prodComm Q I)
  have regroup :
      MeasurePreserving (MeasurableEquiv.curry I Q ℝ)
        (Measure.pi (fun _ : I × Q => σ)) ρ := by
    refine ⟨(MeasurableEquiv.curry I Q ℝ).measurable, ?_⟩
    simpa only [Measure.infinitePi_eq_pi] using
      (Measure.infinitePi_map_curry (fun (_ : I) (_ : Q) => σ))
  have transpose :
      MeasurePreserving (fun x : Q → I → ℝ => fun i : I => fun a : Q => x a i) ν ρ :=
    regroup.comp (swap.comp flatten)
  have wrap_rows :
      MeasurePreserving (fun x : I → Q → ℝ => fun i : I => WithLp.toLp 2 (x i))
        ρ (Measure.pi (fun _ : I => stdGaussian E)) :=
    measurePreserving_pi (fun _ : I => Measure.pi (fun _ : Q => σ))
      (fun _ : I => stdGaussian E) (fun _ => ⟨by fun_prop, map_pi_eq_stdGaussian⟩)
  have actual_joint :
      MeasurePreserving (fun ω : Ω => fun i : I => row i ω) μ
        (Measure.pi (fun _ : I => stdGaussian E)) :=
    wrap_rows.comp (transpose.comp unwrap_columns)

  -- Exact joint product law implies full finite-family independence.
  apply (iIndepFun_iff_map_fun_eq_pi_map (fun i => (row_law i).aemeasurable)).2
  calc
    μ.map (fun ω i => row i ω) = Measure.pi (fun _ : I => stdGaussian E) :=
      actual_joint.map_eq
    _ = Measure.pi (fun i : I => μ.map (row i)) := by
      congr 1
      funext i
      exact (row_law i).map_eq.symm

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceRowIndependence

formulae.label: Actual measurable independent matrix family
formulae.tex: \forall i,\ Y_i\text{ is measurable};\qquad (Y_i)_{i=1}^d\text{ is independent under }\mu.

assumptions: Let \(d,q\in\mathbb N\), \(2q+1<d\), and \(r=q+1\). In particular \(d\ge2\), \(r\ge1\), and \(q=0\) is included.

Write \(\gamma_n=N(0,I_n)\) on real Euclidean \(n\)-space. The outcome space is \(\Omega=(\mathbb R^d)^r\), with the literal column-product probability law \(\mu=\gamma_d^{\otimes r}\). Define \(\Phi_i(\omega)=(\omega_{1,i},\ldots,\omega_{r,i})\in\mathbb R^r\).

The public independence conclusion means factorization for every finite family of Borel row events. The canonical row-law declaration supplies row measurability and Gaussian marginal laws internally; neither law nor independence is a caller-supplied certificate.

For the actual matrix consumer, put \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(t_i[0]=1\), \(t_i[k]=\sqrt2\cos(k\theta_i)\) for \(1\le k\le q\), and \(L=2r+3\log(1000d)\). Lean uses source indices \(i.val+1\) and \(a.val+1\).

Each \(Y_i\) has the displayed literal formula with its own closed cutoff. At entry \(((a,j),(b,k))\), the value inside the cutoff is \(d^{-1}\Phi_i[a]\Phi_i[b]t_i[j]t_i[k]\). Gaussian coordinates come first in both paired indices.

Matrices use their finite real-entry product measurable structure. Both measurability of all \(Y_i\) and full-family independence are proved outputs. The deterministic features vary with \(i\), so no identical-distribution claim for the matrices is made. No Gram, norm, moment, integrability, tail, \(\tau\), or condition-number premise is added.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceRowIndependence

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceRowLaw
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceRowIndependence
set_option autoImplicit false

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.Tests.GaussianComplexityFixedSpectrumSourceRowIndependence

private theorem actual_truncated_matrices_measurable_and_independent
    {d q : ℕ} (hq : 2 * q + 1 < d) :
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun a : Fin (q + 1) => ω a i)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i =>
    (((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - (1 / 2 : ℝ)) * Real.pi) / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      ((Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) → (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) → ℝ) := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun a => row i ω a) (fun a => row i ω a))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  (∀ i : Fin d, Measurable (Y i)) ∧ iIndepFun Y μ := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let Q := Fin (q + 1)
  let I := Fin d
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ I
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ Q
  let Ω := Q → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Q => stdGaussian D)
  let row : I → Ω → E := fun i ω => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun a : Q => ω a i)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let θ : I → ℝ := fun i =>
    (((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - (1 / 2 : ℝ)) * Real.pi) / (d : ℝ)
  let t : I → Q → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let F : I → E → ((Q × Q) → (Q × Q) → ℝ) := fun i x =>
    if ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun a => x a) (fun a => x a))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  let Y : I → Ω → ((Q × Q) → (Q × Q) → ℝ) := fun i ω => F i (row i ω)
  change (∀ i : I, Measurable (Y i)) ∧ iIndepFun Y μ
  have row_law := actual_source_row_marginal_law (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change ∀ i : I, MeasurePreserving (row i) μ (stdGaussian E) at row_law
  have row_independent := actual_source_rows_independent (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change iIndepFun row μ at row_independent

steps.title: Prove measurable images and preserve independence
steps.text: The squared-norm cutoff is a measurable closed event. Inside it, each matrix entry is a polynomial in two row coordinates with fixed scalar coefficients; outside it, the entry is zero. Thus each F_i is measurable into the finite real-entry product space. Compose with row measurability, then apply full-family independence preservation under the separate measurable F_i. The rule requires no injectivity, and the F_i may differ.
steps.formula: F_i(x)_{(a,j),(b,k)}=\frac{x_ax_b\,t_i[j]t_i[k]}d\mathbf1_{\{\|x\|^2\le L\}},\qquad\forall i,\ Y_i\text{ is measurable};\qquad (Y_i)_{i=1}^d\text{ is independent under }\mu.
steps.lean:
have coordinate (a : Q) : Measurable (fun x : E => x a) := by
    dsimp [E]
    fun_prop
  have cutoff : MeasurableSet {x : E | ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ L} :=
    measurableSet_le (by fun_prop) measurable_const
  have F_measurable (i : I) : Measurable (F i) := by
    apply Measurable.ite cutoff
    · apply measurable_pi_lambda
      intro u
      apply measurable_pi_lambda
      intro v
      change Measurable (fun x : E =>
        (d : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((x u.1 * x v.1) * (t i u.2 * t i v.2)))
      exact measurable_const.mul (((coordinate u.1).mul (coordinate v.1)).mul measurable_const)
    · exact measurable_const
  constructor
  · intro i
    exact (F_measurable i).comp (row_law i).measurable
  · exact row_independent.comp F F_measurable

end AutoSamplingTheory.Tests.GaussianComplexityFixedSpectrumSourceRowIndependence
